outline: The Coach's behavior in a soccer scenario is triggered when a teammate is pressured by an opponent. The Coach initiates by moving to an open position, strategically choosing either the left or right side of the field to create a clear passing angle. Upon reaching this position, the Coach either immediately receives the ball if the teammate passes quickly, or waits for the teammate to make the pass. Once the Coach has gained possession of the ball, they then evaluate the opponent's defensive strategy. If the opponent decides to stay with the teammate, the Coach proceeds to shoot the ball towards the goal. Conversely, if the opponent decides to pressure the Coach, the Coach passes the ball back to the teammate to maintain offensive pressure.
